chunks: And from him, from Hammad ibn Shu'ayb, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Witr prayer is three rak'ahs: two separated and one.

key_terms.مَفْصُولَةً: Separated, indicating the two are prayed independently before the third

ai.seo_question: How many rak'ahs are in the Witr prayer and how are they performed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the preferred method of performing Witr as three distinct rak'ahs, emphasizing the separation of the first two to highlight the Sunnah nature of the prayer. In Shia jurisprudence, this structure distinguishes Witr from obligatory prayers and underscores its status as a highly recommended act concluded with a single salam, reflecting the Prophet's practice as transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt.
